direct_pixel_inspection.method: view_image original at 1536x1024; complete saved image directly inspected
direct_pixel_inspection.visible_impression_before_control_compar: A quiet collaborative aircraft servicing photograph. A crouched worker with dark bobbed hair holds a yellow wheel wedge while looking toward the teammate who writes on a clipboard; aircraft and hangar supply a strong work setting. The face is alert and gently appealing rather than theatrically posed. The frame cuts the tire along its left edge and crops much of the secondary worker, while their profile and writing action remain visible.

criteria.evidence: Gray high-wing propeller transport aircraft, large landing gear, olive work coveralls/boots, wedge check and shared clipboard task read as fictional military aviation ground support. No actual service, nationality, rank, qualification or mission success is inferred.

Two distinct crew members share a task: main worker touches the seated chock and turns toward the teammate; the teammate faces inward and marks the clipboard sheet. This supports a staged inspection/acknowledgment moment; it does not prove real before/after responsibility transfer.

The main worker's right arm continues from its shoulder through elbow and wrist to the gloved hand on top of the yellow wedge. The wedge meets the lower tire boundary, and the left arm terminates in the glove resting on her own bent knee.
The second worker's pencil tip meets the inspection paper; the other gloved hand steadies the clipboard over the raised thigh. Exact handwriting and content are not asserted.

The main face retains an oval outline, large dark eyes, small straight nose and rounded lips, with a short dark bob and fine separated fringe. The fictional character's clothing, body and role are independent of the reference; no identity/age inference is made.

The task, two faces, hand-wedge-tire connection and writing contact coexist coherently. However the final prompt and reviewed visibility phrase explicitly requested the entire wheel; its left outline extends beyond the image boundary. Complete authored framing is not realized even though the critical contact is readable.

strengths: Primary face and reciprocal attention form a credible working moment.
Concrete chock contact and pencil contact carry the task rather than clothing alone.
Cool sky and warm hangar spill separate face, worn coveralls and aircraft equipment.
limits: Tire completeness fails at left edge.
The secondary worker is heavily cropped; the main subject dominates, although their profile and recording action remain readable.
Dawn-like color does not independently establish a clock time or chronology.

controls_review.technical_binding: Frozen sensual 1, fetish 0, surreal 0, creativity 1 retained with no overrides.
controls_review.perceived_expression: Subtle attractiveness comes through the attentive face, softly parted mouth and natural working presence. Gloves, coveralls and equipment read as functional details; ordinary physical relations remain coherent. This is a qualitative reading, not a numerical calibration score.
